verdicts.reason: A breaks the layout apart: the flavour pills zigzag at random x positions and widths, the SOLSTICE wordmark sits below the headline, and the CTA is shrunk into the bottom-left corner, so it is buried. B is a coherent centred stack with a prominent CTA, but the headline and subhead run almost edge to edge with no margin, the wordmark is still under the headline, the three pills have mismatched widths and heights, and the stack is cramped.

In A, three oversized pills in a left column outweigh the headline. The subhead is tiny and illegible, the CTA is undersized, and the wordmark is still under the headline, so the hierarchy is inverted. B (same layout as pair 1 B) keeps the headline and CTA dominant, but it has edge-to-edge text with no margins, inconsistent pill sizes and a cramped centre stack.
